purpose: Dated gates the front office and the game builder use. Each date carries its source and whether it was knowable on the career date; a date marked projected is replaced by the actual only when its computation date is reached. Dates and rules only: no 2005-06 result is recorded.

status_values.derived: inferred from cited sources, reasoning given
status_values.design_choice: not verifiable for 2005-06; the simulation's documented choice

sources: Larry Coon, NBA Salary Cap FAQ (2005 CBA), http://www.cbafaq.com/salarycap05.htm, via library/2005/league/nba_2005_cba_rules.json

events.note: Team options, player options, qualifying offers and tenders for 2005-06 are due; the 1999 CBA expires the same day.
events.source: library/2004/league/nba_2004_05_calendar.json#option_and_qualifying_offer_deadline_2005 (Larry Coon, 1999 Salary Cap FAQ, Q34, http://www.cbafaq.com/salarycap99.htm)

events.note: Free agents may negotiate with any club and agree in principle; nothing may be signed. In 2005 the moratorium ran through August 1 so the new CBA (agreed in principle June 21, ratified July 30) could be finalized; the extension is knowable only from June 21, 2005.
events.source: library/2005/league/nba_2005_cba_rules.json dates.july_moratorium_2005 (cbafaq05 Q93; UPI, July 30 and August 1, 2005)
events.trades: no trade during the moratorium (derived from the 2004-05 calendar's rule)

events.note: 2005-06 salary cap $49,500,000 (a fixed figure agreed in the 2005 CBA), tax level $61,700,000 (fixed, set before the season), minimum team salary 75% of the cap ($37,125,000), mid-level exception $5,000,000, bi-annual exception $1,670,000; Charlotte (expansion) cap $37,125,000. Effective August 2. The date is the CBA ratification reported by UPI with the $49.5 million figure; no dated league announcement of the cap was read, so the publication day is derived.
Moratorium over; contracts, offer sheets and trades may be signed; the 2005-06 cap takes effect.

The exact day camps opened in 2005 was not verified; Tuesday October 4 (the first week of October, as in 2004) is the design choice, six days before the first recorded preseason game. Up to 20 players under contract.
events.source: unverified; by analogy with library/2004/league/nba_2004_05_calendar.json#training_camp_opens and library/2005/league/nba_2005_06_preseason_schedule.json (first game 2005-10-10)

events.note: Preseason games, as far as the recorded schedule shows; the source omits games against non-NBA opponents and some neutral sites, so an earlier game cannot be ruled out.
Miami's team option on Wade's fourth season must be exercised by October 31 after his second season (his rookie contract was signed under the 1999 CBA). October 31, 2005 is a Monday.
events.source: Larry Coon, 1999 Salary Cap FAQ, Q38 (http://www.cbafaq.com/salarycap99.htm); library/2004/league/nba_2004_05_calendar.json#wade_fourth_year_option_deadline

events.note: Rosters cut to at most 15 (12 active, up to 3 inactive; at least 13 under contract) before opening night; the deadline is taken as the day before the first game. Under the 2005 CBA the inactive list replaces the injured list and has no minimum stay.
Regular season begins.
Ten-day contracts allowed from January 5 (a Thursday in 2006), as under the 1999 CBA; under the 2005 CBA a club may carry no more ten-day contracts than players on its inactive list.

Last day a non-guaranteed player can be waived and clear waivers before the guarantee date: waivers take 48 hours during the season, so a January 7 release clears on January 9. Same rule as 2003-04 and 2004-05.

All contracts become guaranteed for the rest of the season; a player terminated on or after January 10 is owed the rest of the season's salary. The January 10 date is sourced for the 1999 CBA; the 2005 CBA keeps January 10 as its in-season gate (exceptions prorate and rookie-scale amounts reduce from January 10), so carrying it forward is derived.
events.source: Larry Coon, 1999 Salary Cap FAQ, Q90 and Q96 (http://www.cbafaq.com/salarycap99.htm); library/2005/league/nba_2005_cba_rules.json exceptions.january_10_proration (cbafaq05)

events.note: All-Star Weekend in Houston; the All-Star Game is Sunday February 19, 2006 at the Toyota Center (Rookie Challenge Friday February 17). No regular-season games February 17-20.
Trade deadline (Thursday). The 3 p.m. ET hour is carried from 2003-04 (derived).
events.source: Silver Chips (Montgomery Blair HS), 'Trades shake up NBA landscape', February 2006: 'the Feb. 23 trade deadline' (https://silverchips.mbhs.edu/content/trades-shake-up-nba-landscape-24016/); https://www.basketball-reference.com/leagues/NBA_2006_transactions.html (multi-club trades dated February 23, 2006)

events.note: A player waived after March 1 is ineligible for the playoff roster of any club that signs him for the rest of the season. Sourced for the 1999 CBA; carried forward unchanged.
events.source: Larry Coon, 1999 Salary Cap FAQ, Q53 and Q96 (http://www.cbafaq.com/salarycap99.htm); library/2003/league/nba_1999_in_season_rules.json

events.note: Under the 2005 CBA the tax level ($61.7 million for 2005-06) is fixed before the season and levied every season on team salary as of the club's last regular-season game; no after-season trigger applies. The date is the last regular-season day.
Last regular-season games.
First-round games begin; four series open April 22 and four April 23. Bracket, seeding and dates: library/2005/league/nba_2005_06_playoff_rules.json.
NBA Finals window, 2-3-2: Game 1 June 8; Games 5 and 6, if needed, June 18 and 20 (sourced); Game 7, if needed, June 22 (derived from the Thursday pattern).
2006 NBA Draft (two rounds; first draft under the 2005 CBA's age limit).
Team options, player options, qualifying offers and tenders for 2006-07 are due; the June 30 date is carried from the 1999 CBA (the 2005 CBA keeps qualifying offers due June 30).
Free agents may negotiate and agree in principle; nothing may be signed until the 2006-07 cap is set.
Moratorium lifted at 12:01 a.m. Wednesday July 12 after clubs were told the 2006-07 cap late Tuesday July 11. The 2006-07 cap figure is not recorded here and must not be used before July 11, 2006.
events.source: Sportsbook Review forum repost of a July 2006 wire report, 'Salary cap for 2006-07 season set' (https://www.sportsbookreview.com/forum/nba-basketball-betting/10416-salary-cap-for-2006-07-season-set-at-53-135m); secondary source
